partial_results: Two energy levels suffice for both refined trace bounds
Both bounds hold in every finite dimension and at all word lengths whenever either observable has at most two distinct levels, with arbitrary multiplicities. The general lower bound remains open.
Rank-seven nonlocal magic on three qubits per party

All rank-seven spectra on two three-qubit registers, three larger-register regions and an unbounded-rank two-exception family have proofs. Separate project reviewers checked the reductions and exact certificates. External review is pending.
The written proof covers all photon-number distributions. Lean checks the arithmetic induction.
The proof covers pure and mixed states in the two-level optical subspace.
The paper excludes orders and derives a sharp lower threshold on the optical qubit.
The sparse-state argument restricts possible counterexamples within levels zero to five.
An interval certificate covers a continuum of weak cubic gates with arbitrary Gaussian processing.
The argument restricts a witness search by classifying coordinate sets with positive compression.
Complete finite search certificates establish the reported support maxima for the specified instances.

exclusions.title: Weak multimode bound
exclusions.detail: The derivation passes mathematical review. The classical STFT change-of-window inequality already gives the claimed constant. The sharp parent question remains open.

exclusions.title: Finite three-factor BMV certificates
exclusions.detail: Two exact implementations agreed across 26 word counts. A preexisting formal theorem already covers them all. The project records one replication.

screened_leads.captured_question: This disproves the strong form of a conjecture presented by Ho and Hsieh stating that the expressivity of VQCS on $L$ qubits saturates at $L/2$ layers.
screened_leads.title: Strong Ho–Hsieh circuit saturation conjecture
screened_leads.detail: Jiang’s four-qubit counterexample already disproves the strong claim captured by our scanner. The source distinguishes a narrower ground-state question.
